prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: hospital medication dispensing/returns: order intake, pharmacy prep/verification, cold chain, tube transport, ward cabinets, returns, dose exceptions. Aliases: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Elements: Gateway (validates patient/product/dose/route/timing before release; rejects incomplete updates, keeps reason; Order Reconciliation Snapshot; routes to review). Robot (uses Snapshot to compare requested qty vs dispense events/cabinet balances by order ID; checks active/authorization; Priority Refill Tote Tag; presents package to Station; on exception stops pick, holds package, keeps scan data). Station (compares order vs scanned product/strength/qty, blocks mismatch; Batch Release Note; Dose Exception Review Slip). Cooler (per-compartment timestamped temperature history, approved upper/lower limits, alarms; calibrated probes log probe ID/calibration; stock tracked by medication/lot/expiry; excursion or probe loss marks stock ineligible, preserved in place pending assessment; uses Cold Chain Handoff Card to compare custody time vs history; retains lot disposition, blocks ineligible selection; logs access user/time/stock; monitors door-open duration; alarms persist offline, local records retained). East/West Tube Dispatch Consoles (capsules; Tube Route Exception Ticket). Pneumatic Tube Network (segment unavailable until tested). North/South Ward Cabinet Controllers (Ready for Dispense, Out of Service; North: tote tag ward check, blocks held transactions, applies North Ward rules; versioned reviewed config (effective time, approver) defines locations, product IDs, thresholds, roles, limits; availability=last count+movements; min/max guide replenishment, never override clinical restriction; authenticated role; high-risk extra confirmation; rejects location/identity mismatch; no approved config→block routine dispensing, report. South reports failed lock/unrecognized access). Return Kiosk (Return Bin Audit Label). Actors: Clinical Pharmacist (Review Slip; approves/rejects; excursion disposition release/quarantine/discard; inconclusive→hold, escalate). Pharmacy Technician (prep; Cold Chain Handoff Card; no unresolved discrepancy before replenishment; no clinical decisions). Medication Safety Officer (Diversion Review Packet to IT Operations Specialist). IT Operations Specialist (reviews logs without changing disposition; software/connectivity

New part:
S183: East Tube Dispatch Console maintains the approved route map and the current availability status of supported pneumatic segments.
S184: East Tube Dispatch Console checks the selected route against the destination cabinet, current network availability, and approved routing configuration before releasing a capsule.
S185: The console confirms that the destination is reachable and that the route does not include a segment reported unavailable.
S186: Route selection uses the destination identifier and the latest approved configuration version rather than an operator-entered sequence of segments.
S187: Before dispatch, the console checks for conflicting capsule movements and confirms that required interlocks are satisfied.
S188: The Pneumatic Tube Network reports segment status, transfer progress, and delivery confirmation to the dispatch console.
S189: If route status is stale or incomplete, the console holds the capsule and displays the condition for operator review.
S190: A loss of communication with a route sensor prevents the console from treating the affected segment as available.
S191: An interruption during transit is recorded with the capsule identifier, last confirmed location, and time of the interruption.
S192: The console alerts a Pharmacy Technician when a transfer stops progressing or cannot be confirmed at its destination.
S193: After recovery, the console requires refreshed segment status and an approved route decision before dispatch resumes.
S194: Route and temperature records retain timestamps and equipment identifiers to support operational review and investigation.
S195: The Pharmacy Verification Station serves as the final controlled checkpoint before a medication is made available for dispensing.
S196: The Clinical Pharmacist compares the active medication order with the product, strength, dosage form, dose, route, and scheduled time.
S197: The Clinical Pharmacist also confirms that the patient identifiers and pharmacy label agree with the authorized order.
S198: The Pharmacy Technician checks package integrity, lot identification, and expiry before presenting the medication for verification.
S199: For designated high-risk medications, an independent second check is completed and recorded before authorization.
S200: Any mismatch places the medication on hold until the discrepancy is resolved by an authorized pharmacy professional.
S201: The verification record captures the approving staff identity, time, and medication identifiers for later review.
S202: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot remains inhibited from completing a dispense until the required pharmacy authorization is present.
S203: The Clinical Pharmacist resolves unclear or conflicting order details through the Medication Order Gateway before authorizing release.
S204: The South Ward Cabinet Controller receives the release note and applies its own approved cabinet configuration before enabling any compartment.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
